name: Oxford Quantum Circuits
description: Oxford Quantum Circuits (OQC) is a UK-based quantum computing company spun out of the University of Oxford, developing superconducting quantum processors based on its proprietary Coaxmon three-dimensional qubit architecture. OQC offers quantum-compute-as-a-service and has deployed systems in commercial data centres, with a published roadmap targeting 50,000 logical qubits by 2034.

products.name: Coaxmon Quantum Processors
products.description: Superconducting quantum processors based on proprietary 3D Coaxmon qubit architecture for improved coherence

products.name: OQC Cloud
products.description: Quantum-compute-as-a-service platform providing cloud access to OQC superconducting quantum systems

news.title: Oxford Quantum Circuits raises $100M for quantum compute-as-a-service
news.excerpt: OQC announced that Japanese VC fund SBI Investment is leading OQC's $100 million round. The company also announced the public availability of OQC Toshiko, the world's first enterprise-ready quantum computing platform.

news.title: OQC and Riverlane Launch UK's First Quantum Error Corrected Testbed Integrated with HPC
news.excerpt: OQC and Riverlane launch the UK's first quantum error corrected testbed integrated with high-performance computing.

news.title: OQC unveils 500+ qubit wafer-scale packaging architecture
news.excerpt: New packaging approach houses over 500 superconducting qubits on a single 3-inch die while preserving coherence and readout fidelity.

news.title: Oxford Quantum Circuits raises £260 million in Europe's largest private quantum funding round
news.excerpt: OQC closed a £260 million Series C led by Bullhound Capital with participation from the British Business Bank, which committed £100 million, to expand data-centre quantum deployments globally and accelerate development of its superconducting GENESIS processor platform.
